note: Early, DaT-SPECT-confirmed PD; prasinezumab (humanised 9E4, validated in Thy1-α-syn mice) and cinpanemab (BIIB054, validated in PFF-inoculated mice) both missed phase 2 primaries, and no accessible primary source sets the mouse prediction beside the patient result.
label: Parkinson's (anti-α-syn)

engagement.note: 9E4, prasinezumab's murine parent, entered the CNS and bound α-syn-laden cells in Thy1-α-syn mice.
engagement.short: 9E4 enters mouse CNS, binds α-syn cells
engagement.quote: In vivo studies demonstrated that 9E4 traffics into the CNS, binds to cells that display α-syn accumulation and promotes α-syn clearance via the lysosomal pathway.

engagement.note: Prasinezumab cut free serum α-syn 97% in PD patients and reached CSF at 0.3% of serum; brain engagement inferred, never measured against the mouse.
engagement.quote: Mean cerebrospinal fluid PRX002 concentration increased with PRX002 dose and was approximately 0.3% relative to serum across all dose cohorts.
engagement.reason: Brain engagement never measured vs mouse
engagement.judgement: Peripheral binding (free serum α-syn −97%; BIIB054 plasma complexes saturated in PD participants, Brys 2019) is a patient result the mouse never predicted; the mouse claim was CNS entry and clearance, which no trial measured. Not 'same'. Abstract only: the PMC record for this paper carries no body text.

dose.note: Mouse CNS entry of 9E4 was the only exposure prediction behind prasinezumab; no human exposure target was derived from it.
dose.short: Mouse CNS entry, no human target
dose.quote: This study investigated whether passive immunization with a novel monoclonal α-syn antibody (9E4) against the C-terminus (CT) of α-syn was able to cross into the CNS and ameliorate the deficits associated with α-syn accumulation.

dose.model: α-syn PFF-inoculated mice; CSF-saturation PK projection
dose.note: SPARK's top dose came from a projected CSF-saturation exposure, not mouse efficacy; SPARK showed no dose-response and nobody compared exposures.
dose.quote: exposure equivalent to the 45-mg/kg dose level has been set as the highest exposure for the currently ongoing phase II clinical trial of BIIB054, based on the projections for aggregated α-syn to BIIB054 binding saturation in CSF.
dose.reason: Exposure target never checked against mouse
dose.judgement: Human exposure was set from a CSF aggregate-binding saturation projection, not from the mouse-efficacious exposure in Weihofen 2019; SPARK (results posted 2021-11-23) found no dose-response at 250/1250/3500 mg, and no source compares the two. Schenk 2017 (doi:10.1002/mds.26878, healthy volunteers) says of prasinezumab that CNS penetration 'remains to be demonstrated ... as is predicted by preclinical studies'. Quote is a verbatim clause (non-breaking hyphen in '45-mg/kg' normalised).

efficacy.note: 9E4 reduced water-maze deficits and calpain-cleaved α-syn in Thy1-α-syn mice, the basis for prasinezumab.
efficacy.quote: In this study we demonstrate that 9E4 was effective at reducing behavioral deficits in the water maze, moreover, immunization with 9E4 reduced the accumulation of calpain-cleaved α-syn in axons and synapses and the associated neurodegenerative deficits.

efficacy.note: BIIB054 slowed pathology spread, rescued motor deficits and preserved striatal DAT in three PFF-inoculated mouse models.
efficacy.quote: In efficacy studies in three different mouse models with intracerebrally inoculated preformed α-syn fibrils, BIIB054 treatment attenuated the spreading of α-syn pathology, rescued motor impairments, and reduced the loss of dopamine transporter density in dopaminergic terminals in striatum.
efficacy.judgement: Second untested row added because cinpanemab's pivotal model differs from prasinezumab's. Abstract only (Elsevier paywall); epub 2018-10-28, print Neurobiol Dis 124:276 (2019).

efficacy.note: SPARK (cinpanemab) and PASADENA (prasinezumab) both missed MDS-UPDRS and DaT-SPECT primaries; no primary source sets this against the mouse rescue.
efficacy.quote: In participants with early Parkinson's disease, the effects of cinpanemab on clinical measures of disease progression and changes in DaT-SPECT imaging did not differ from those of placebo over a 52-week period.
efficacy.judgement: By substance this is a contra: PFF mice promised slowed spread, motor rescue and DAT preservation; SPARK (NCT03318523, results posted 2021-11-23) showed none on MDS-UPDRS or DaT-SPECT, and PASADENA (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2202867, NCT03100149, results posted 2021-02-08) likewise missed (−2.0 and −0.6 points, P=0.24/0.72). But the NEJM Discussions are the only place the comparison could be stated and both returned HTTP 403 and are not in PMC/Europe PMC, so under rule 2 it stays untested with comparison_stated=false. Flip to contra if a reader with NEJM access confirms a Discussion sentence contrasting the mouse result with the trial.

efficacy.note: PADOVA (prasinezumab on symptomatic therapy) missed its primary too, HR 0.84 for motor progression; still no model-vs-patient comparison in print.
efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint was not met; the primary analysis showed a non-significant delay in motor progression with prasinezumab versus placebo (hazard ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·69-1·01]; p=0·066)
efficacy.judgement: Separate row (same status) because PADOVA is a distinct comparison trial with its own registry date. PADOVA's HR 0.84 (p=0.066) and the PASADENA post hoc (Pagano 2024, doi:10.1038/s41591-024-02886-y, open access, no mouse mention) are the 'motor-progression signal' that keeps prasinezumab in phase 3 (PARAISO, NCT07174310); none of these sources mentions the mouse. Lancet full text paywalled; abstract only. Prasinezumab's model was dosed with 9E4, not the product.

safety.note: Tox was silent on vascular events; a BIIB054-dosed volunteer had a silent infarct the authors could not attribute; SPARK later listed headache, nasopharyngitis, falls.
safety.quote: neither the proposed mechanism of action of BIIB054 nor the results of preclinical toxicology studies suggest that stroke or other types of vascular disease are likely to be adverse effects of BIIB054
safety.judgement: Brys 2019 does set tox beside the event (comparison_stated true) but leaves it open ('could not be excluded'); the event was a 5-mm asymptomatic cerebrovascular accident in a 135 mg/kg healthy volunteer, 3x SPARK's top dose. Prasinezumab's infusion reactions (19%/34%, Pagano 2022 abstract) are the class's real safety finding and no source compares them with tox, so neither 'same' nor 'contra' is supportable. Tox species and first-use year not stated in any source read; 2019 is the first mention.
